name: Grocery-anchored shopping center
summary: Neighborhood center (≈60,000–150,000 SF) with a 40,000–65,000 SF supermarket anchor plus in-line shops and outparcels. The landlord typically delivers the anchor as a shell/pad (grocer funds refrigeration and fixtures) and builds a large parking field. No public development budget was retrieved; cost is derived from RLB strip/center ranges and RSMeans supermarket/store models.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per GSF; grocers commonly require 4.5–5.5/1,000 in their leases (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived blend. Anchor: RSMeans 2019 supermarket model $129.75–141.15 (complete basic building excl. site, e3) × ≈1.3 = $169–183; landlord shell ≈ 80% → ≈$140. In-line: same build-up as retail-strip (≈$140 shell). Plus sitework ≈$35–40/SF for 4.5–5/1,000 parking. → ≈$175. Larger buildings than a strip lower $/SF slightly (RSMeans supermarket at 44,000 SF ≈ 0.95× the 8,000-SF store model, e3 vs e6). Cross-check: RLB 2026 strip Dallas $200–270 and center Dallas $215–355 (e1, e2). Low = $120, High = $265 (≈RLB center Dallas midpoint). RSMeans model escalation 2019→2026 ≈ ×1.3, inferred from RSMeans' own office 2–4 story model: 2019 total $187.02 (open) / $204.43 (union) vs. 2026 national $253.63 (BD+C) = ×1.24–1.36. This is only used to compare evidence; the build script escalates from the stated dollarYear.

scope.notes: Landlord shell for anchor and in-line plus on-site work; excludes grocer fit-out/refrigeration, in-line tenant fit-out, land, soft costs, off-site road work.

systemSplit.method: Derived from the retail-strip split with sitework raised to 27% (larger parking fields, truck court, detention).

lineItems.name: Grocery anchor fit-out incl. refrigeration (if landlord-funded)

cost.method: Derived: refrigeration ≈ $30–90/SF of refrigerated area (_blocks/specialty-mep.json cold-storage-refrigeration) over ≈40% of the store, plus interior finishes, lighting and fixtures ≈ $50–100/SF of store. Qty = anchor share of GLA ≈ 50%.

lineItems.notes: Normally the grocer's cost; turn on for build-to-suit deals.

cost.method: Cushman 2026 in-line fit-out $157 national, $120 Midwest, $217 Northern California (e5); qty = in-line share ≈ 40% of GLA.

lineItems.name: In-line landlord TI allowance

cost.method: Derived judgment: 10–40% of the $157/SF in-line fit-out (e5).

lineItems.notes: Typical for new centers; turn off if delivering turnkey.

lineItems.name: Outparcel pad preparation (grading, utilities stub, access)

cost.method: Derived judgment: mass grading, utility stubs and shared drive access per 1-acre pad.

pctOfHard.method: Derived: A/E 5–7% (RSMeans supermarket model carries 7%), platting/permits/traffic study 1–3%, survey/geotech 1%, insurance/legal 2%, developer fee 3–5%, leasing 3–5%. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 4 points to remove the developer fee (3–5%). The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Anchor lease negotiations and traffic/turn-lane studies are typical type-specific soft items.

design.method: Simple commercial shells: low design contingency.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Min ≈ $120 × 1.12; max ≈ RLB center median high ($412) — all-in with soft costs rarely exceeds it for open-air neighborhood centers.

source.title: North America Quarterly Construction Cost Report, Q3 2026 (Indicative Construction Costs table)

evidence.quote: Indicative construction costs, Retail Shopping — Strip: Dallas 200–270; Phoenix 135–220; Charlotte 205–290 (USD/SF GFA, hard construction costs).
evidence.scopeNotes: Values are the Dallas column; Phoenix 135–220; 18-US-city median 202.5–295. RLB does not say whether strip figures are shell-only or include sitework.

source.title: North America Quarterly Construction Cost Report, Q3 2026 (Indicative Construction Costs table)

evidence.quote: Indicative construction costs, Retail Shopping — Center: Dallas 215–355; Austin 210–345; Charlotte 220–370 (USD/SF GFA).
evidence.scopeNotes: Values are the Dallas column; 18-US-city median 227.5–412.5. "Center" = larger shopping center (format not defined).

source.title: Construction Cost Estimates for a Supermarket in National, US (2019 RSMeans data)

evidence.quote: Supermarket ... Floor Area (S.F.): 44,000 ... SubTotal 100% $112.92 ... Contractor Fees (General Conditions,Overhead,Profit) 25% $28.23 (union); open shop SubTotal $103.80, fees $25.95
evidence.scopeNotes: Basic-component model building, excludes sitework. Hard = SubTotal + contractor fees (open $129.75, union $141.15); architectural fee 7% excluded.

source.title: 2022 Project Costs — 50 17 00 Project Costs per S.F.

evidence.quote: Retail, Total Project Costs per S.F.: 1/4 = 96, Median = 171, 3/4 = 325 (Plumbing 5.45%, Mechanical 6.15%, Electrical 11.25% medians).
evidence.scopeNotes: Completed retail buildings, January 2022 national dollars, incl. contractor OH&P; sitework scope not stated.

source.title: U.S. Retail Fit Out Cost Guide (2026)

evidence.quote: National in-line retail fit out costs averaged $157 per square foot (psf) in 2026 ... Northern California ($217 psf) ... the Midwest ($120 psf) and Southeast ($126 psf) remain the most cost-effective.
evidence.scopeNotes: Tenant in-line store fit-out (not landlord shell).

evidence.scopeNotes: Basic-component model building, excludes sitework. Hard = SubTotal + contractor fees (open $134.49, union $151.29); architectural fee 8% excluded.

evidence.quote: Square Foot Costs: Office Building, 2-4 Story — National Average Q2 2026 $253.63.
evidence.scopeNotes: Used only to infer RSMeans model escalation 2019→2026 (vs. 2019 office 2–4 story model total $187.02–204.43).

evidence.quote: ONE-STORY FLEX OFFICE BUILDINGS $103 to $122/SF ... Cost includes $16 to $22/sf for sitework, assuming five spaces/1,000 sf in a surface parking lot.
evidence.scopeNotes: One-story building with 5/1,000 surface parking — closest published proxy for retail sitework per building SF (Austin $21–30, Dallas $23–37 for the same building).

openQuestions: No public grocery-anchored center development budget (TIF/development agreement) retrieved — search budget exhausted. Such a budget would validate the derived mid and the anchor-vs-inline split.
